title: Indonesia Needs to Do More to Tackle the Region’s Transboundary Haze Problem
gist: Severe 2026 forest and peatland fires in Indonesia have spread transboundary haze across Southeast Asia, making Kuching the world's most polluted large city in early September, triggering a state of emergency in Sarawak's Serian district and school closures in Metro Manila. The author argues President Prabowo Subianto bears key responsibility and must lead better haze management within ASEAN.

insights.claim: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto is the key ASEAN leader who can and should improve haze management, since most of the current Southeast Asian haze stems from fires in Indonesia.
insights.so_what: Haze is becoming a diplomatic liability for Indonesia, raising pressure for enforcement against land-clearing fires linked to plantation sectors.
insights.quote: The current haze situation affecting Southeast Asia is, to a certain extent, a reflection of his leadership and management
insights.locator: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto is the key
insights.speaker: Edmund Lim

insights.claim: Indonesia's forests and peatlands have burned substantially in 2026, causing suffering for millions across Southeast Asia, including in West Kalimantan's North Kayong regency.
insights.so_what: Peatland fires carry large carbon and public-health costs, affecting regional productivity and Indonesia's climate commitments.
insights.speaker: Edmund Lim

insights.claim: In early September 2026, Kuching had the worst air quality of any large city on earth, and Malaysia declared a state of emergency in Sarawak's Serian district as the Air Pollutant Index exceeded 500.
insights.so_what: Emergency-level pollution disrupts economic activity and aviation in Malaysian Borneo and fuels bilateral friction with Indonesia.
insights.quote: In early September, Kuching had the worst air quality of any large city on earth.
insights.speaker: Edmund Lim

insights.claim: The Philippines closed schools throughout Metro Manila and more than 12 provinces due to the haze, and ASEAN's regional haze monitor reached level three, the most severe on its scale.
insights.so_what: The haze's reach to the Philippines shows the crisis is region-wide, raising the stakes for ASEAN's transboundary haze mechanisms.
insights.quote: The regional haze monitor in ASEAN reached level three, the most severe on the scale.
insights.speaker: Edmund Lim
